findings.title: `include_website_name` is missing `?` and is not listed in `untrusted_attributes`
findings.body: `UserSerializer` defines `def include_website_name` (without a trailing `?`), whereas ActiveModel::Serializers checks `include_<attr>?` to decide whether to serialize an attribute. Because the `?` is missing, `website_name` is always included in the serialized JSON (as `nil` when the user has no website). In addition, `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` so that it is hidden for TL0 users when viewed by anonymous visitors (`scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`), but `website_name` is not added to `untrusted_attributes`. As a result, a TL0 user's website domain/path is leaked via `website_name` to anonymous users even when `website` itself is suppressed. Adding `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` (and removing the broken `include_website_name` method, since `untrusted_attributes` already defines `include_website_name?`) fixes both issues.

findings.title: `website_name` is not updated on the client after saving user preferences
findings.body: Previously, `websiteName` was a computed property on the controller observing `model.website`, so editing and saving `website` in user preferences immediately updated the displayed website name on the profile page. Now that `website_name` is computed server-side in `UserSerializer`, `User#save` (around line 210, where `self.set('bio_excerpt', data.user.bio_excerpt)` is updated from the PUT response) does not copy `data.user.website_name` back onto the model. After a user updates their `website` in preferences and navigates back to their profile without a full page reload, the profile will continue displaying the stale `website_name` (or nothing if they previously had no website).
